hooks.text: A wasp slips one egg inside a cockroach’s egg case. What happens next turns the roach eggs into food.
hooks.payoff: Explain how the ensign wasp’s egg develops into a larva that feeds on the cockroach eggs inside the case.

hooks.text: A dozen or more cockroach eggs can feed a single young wasp. How does it get inside their egg case?
hooks.payoff: Reveal that the female ensign wasp places one egg inside the case, putting her developing young among its food.

hooks.text: Eating cockroach eggs is how this wasp grows up. Its mother puts it right inside the case where those eggs are developing.
hooks.payoff: Identify the ensign wasp and explain that the mother deposits an egg, whose larva then feeds within the cockroach egg case.

hooks.text: Laying one extra egg can change what happens inside a cockroach egg case. That egg belongs to a wasp.
hooks.payoff: Explain how the added ensign wasp egg produces a larva that consumes the developing cockroach eggs.

hooks.text: This wasp eats cockroach eggs when it’s young, and it won’t sting or bite you as an adult. Its relationship with roaches starts inside their egg case.
hooks.payoff: Introduce the ensign wasp, distinguish its harmlessness to people from its larva’s feeding, and explain how the female places an egg inside a cockroach egg case.
